Name: HEPA H14/13 Filter
Description: The BRS HEPA H14/13 Filter is a replacement HEPA filter element from Alveo3D, made to fit the RatPack filter module. It is available in two sizes: Small (124x124x44mm, H13, 99.95% at MPPS 0.3µm, ~600h lifespan) and Large (150x150x50mm external, 160x160x50mm frame, H14, 99.995% at MPPS 0.3µm, ~900h lifespan). The honeycomb element uses cotton, PP and PET media with a PU foam joint seal, rated to 55 m3/h max airflow, 120 Pa max air resistance, and 0-60 °C working temperature. It captures ultrafine particles only — there is no carbon stage, so it does not address VOCs on its own and is best paired with a carbon filter such as the Nevermore or the CF80 cartridge. It was sold out on the BRS store at time of check.
Verdict Label: The correct H13/H14 replacement element for the RatPack — high efficiency, long service life
Cons:
HEPA only — captures particles, not VOCs; no carbon stage, so pair with carbon filtration for fumes
Sold out on the live BRS store at time of check (2026-11-13)
Two sizes/classes (Small H13 vs Large H14) — must order the size matching your RatPack housing
Hour-rated consumable (~600-900h) — needs periodic replacement
Working temperature limited to 0-60 °C
Pros:
True HEPA H14 (99.995%) / H13 (99.95%) at MPPS 0.3µm — very high particulate efficiency
Drop-in replacement element for the RatPack filter module
Long service life: ~600h (Small/H13) / ~900h (Large/H14)
PU foam joint seal and honeycomb construction; rated to 55 m3/h max airflow, 120 Pa max resistance
Two sizes cover RatPack small and large housings

Name: Exhaust Filter
Description: The Voron Exhaust Filter is the official BOM air filtration design for the V2.4, mounting at the rear exhaust panel and routing through a large activated carbon bed before venting externally. It's a sound design and ships with large carbon capacity, but community consensus has largely moved toward the Nevermore Micro for new builds: recirculating air through carbon inside the chamber eliminates VOCs more completely than venting filtered air out of the room. Most build guides now recommend printing the Nevermore alongside or instead of the stock exhaust filter.
Verdict Label: Stock BOM starting point — functional, but most builds upgrade to Nevermore for recirculation
Cons:
Exhaust-only design — vents filtered air outside the enclosure rather than recirculating it
Requires external exhaust routing (hose/duct to window or outside) for meaningful effectiveness
Does not keep VOCs inside the enclosure for elimination — if you vent inside the room, the carbon helps but imperfectly
Superseded by the Nevermore Micro for most builds — recirculation is a fundamentally better approach for enclosed printing
Only designed for Voron 2.4 exhaust panel geometry
Pros:
Official Voron Design exhaust filter — part of the base V2.4 BOM
Large carbon bed for substantial media capacity
Simple design — mounts directly to the V2.4 rear exhaust panel cutout
Uses the existing 60mm exhaust fan already on the V2.4 BOM — no additional hardware required
High community familiarity — documented extensively in the V2.4 build guides

Name: CF80 Filtration
Description: The BRS CF80 is a heavy-duty, plug-and-play air filtration unit for the RatRig V-Core 3.1, combining a HEPA filter with a refillable 250g activated carbon cartridge (V2.5) in a single housing. Two 80x38mm Sunon PWM fans drive chamber air through the carbon bed and HEPA stage, with input and output flows oriented to the upper chamber to avoid turbulence over the print area. BRS publishes measured closed-chamber data after 2h of ABS printing: VOC 0-1 on a 0-10 scale (vs 6-7 without the filter), formaldehyde under 0.0001 mg/m3, and PM2.5 under 1 µg/m3. An optional beta servo flap automates open-loop exhaust (PLA/PETG) versus closed-loop recirculation (ABS/ASA/PA/PC) via Klipper. The cartridge lasts 12-24 months depending on usage and refills for under 20 EUR; the design files (STEP + STL) are published free on Printables. It is a premium-priced complete system, not a DIY print project, and it was sold out on the BRS store at time of check.
Verdict Label: Premium plug-and-play HEPA + carbon system for V-Core 3.1 — superb measured filtration, at a premium price
Cons:
Premium price (on file $411.10; live store lists EUR 319-369) — far above DIY Nevermore/BentoBox builds
Sold out on the live BRS store at time of check (2026-11-13)
Designed around the V-Core 3.1 — fitment on other enclosed printers is not documented
Servo flap is a beta module that may need fine-tuning (per BRS)
250g carbon bed is still a consumable — cartridge needs refilling every 12-24 months
Pros:
Combined HEPA + 250g activated carbon cartridge in one unit — captures fine particles and VOCs together
Measured closed-chamber results after 2h ABS printing: VOC 0-1 (vs 6-7 without), CH2O under 0.0001 mg/m3, PM2.5 under 1 µg/m3
Refillable V2.5 cartridge with 12-24 month lifespan; refills under 20 EUR
Dual 80x38mm Sunon PWM fans supplied, wiring and DC jack installed — sold as a complete unit
Optional servo flap switches between recirculating closed loop (ABS/ASA/PA/PC) and exhaust open loop (PLA/PETG)
Design files (STEP + STL) published free on Printables; V-Core 3.1 compatible

Name: RatPack HEPA Filter Module
Description: The RatPack is RatRig's in-chamber air filter module for V-Core printers, combining a HEPA H13/H14 pleated filter from Alveo 3D with coconut activated carbon granules to capture both ultrafine particles and VOCs. A 120x32 24V blower recirculates chamber air through the filter, with native RatOS and Klipper integration for automated fan control before, during and after prints. It comes in Small (124x124x44mm filter, 600-hour service life) and Large (160x160x53mm, H14, 900-hour service life) versions; printed enclosure and mount parts are required but not included. Price basis: $48.99 (Small variant, smallest size; Large is $64.99).
Verdict Label: RatRig's integrated in-chamber HEPA+carbon filter — polished and plug-and-play for V-Core builds, at a premium over DIY options
Cons:
Printed parts required but not included — enclosure and mounts must be printed first
Premium price vs DIY options: $64.99 (Large) / $48.99 (Small) before printed parts, vs ~$8-15 BOM for Nevermore Micro / BentoBox
Carbon is impregnated in the HEPA filter, not a refillable loose bed — the whole filter element is replaced when exhausted
Designed for RatRig V-Core — other printers depend on the flexible mounts fitting their enclosure
Pros:
Two-stage filtration in one unit: HEPA H13 (Small) / H14 (Large) pleated filter plus coconut activated carbon granules for VOCs and odours
In-chamber recirculation — scrubs chamber air during the print and for 300 seconds after, so fumes are cleared before the printer is opened
Native RatOS and Klipper integration — fan triggers and automations configurable in firmware
Two sizes: Small fits V-Core 3 and 300mm V-Core 4, Large suits 400-500mm V-Core 4; flexible mounts adapt it to other printers
Long filter service life: 600 hours (Small) / 900 hours (Large)
Open source — STLs and CAD under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

Name: Nevermore MAX Printed Parts
Description: The Nevermore MAX Printed Parts kit is MPP's printed-parts set for the Nevermore MAX, the large external recirculating filter for 300mm+ builds — the biggest unit in the Nevermore family. Parts are printed in LDO ABS (1,133g of filament, about 56 hours of print time) in black with an accent colour of your choice. The completed unit holds roughly a kilo of activated carbon plus four HEPA filters, driven by a 70mm blower, for far longer service intervals than a Micro. Fans, carbon, HEPA filters, hardware and panels are sourced separately per the BOM, and note the design itself is archived — the StealthMax is its successor and the current recommendation.
Verdict Label: Archived MAX design, superseded by StealthMax — kit saves 56 hours of printing, but fans, carbon and HEPA are extra
Cons:
Printed parts only — fan, ~1kg carbon, 4 HEPA filters, hardware and panels are all sourced separately, so the true build cost is well above $159.99
Archived work-in-progress design superseded by the StealthMax — the StealthMax is the current recommendation for 300mm+ builds
Requires a 300x300mm bed minimum and an external mounting location — much larger footprint than under-bed filters
Printed on demand — up to 5 days to ship (typically 2-3 days)
Pros:
Saves ~56 hours of printing and 1,133g of filament — the MAX frame is notoriously warp-prone in ABS
Parts printed in LDO ABS to proper specs (0.2mm layers, 4 wall loops, 40% adaptive cubic infill)
Highest-capacity Nevermore — ~1kg of carbon plus built-in HEPA, far longer service intervals than a Micro
Accent colour of your choice included; ASA-CF option available
Open-source GPLv3 design with a full BOM on GitHub

Name: Nevermore Mini / StealthMax HEPA Filter
Description: A replacement HEPA filter element (190mm x 45mm) for the Nevermore Mini and StealthMax S. It adds the particulate-capture stage the carbon-only Mini lacks, catching ultrafine particles down to 2.5µm and below, and drops into the HEPA cartridge variants of the Mini and the StealthMax S. At $4.49 it is a cheap consumable — replace it when you change the carbon.
Verdict Label: Cheap consumable — the correct HEPA element for the Mini / StealthMax S
Cons:
HEPA only — captures particles but does nothing for VOCs on its own; it complements the carbon bed, it does not replace it
Element only — needs the HEPA cartridge variant of the Mini / StealthMax S housing to mount in
No filtration grade published (no H13/H14 rating stated) — efficiency class unverified
Pros:
Correct-fit HEPA element (190 x 45mm) for the Nevermore Mini / StealthMax S
Adds the particulate-filtration stage the carbon-only Mini lacks — captures ultrafine particles
Very cheap at $4.49 — negligible running cost
In stock at Fabreeko

Name: Activated Carbon Pellets
Description: Bulk activated carbon pellets sold by NorthPrint3D as refill media for 3D-printer air filters — the carbon bed for Nevermore and Rebreather designs on Voron and Annex printers, and the BentoBox for Bambu Lab printers. Steam-activated anthracite carbon, 4mm diameter pellets, 1250–1300 m²/g surface area, CTC efficiency 80 minimum, acid-free with no sucrose-based binders. Sold as a 400g bag (~850mL volume) — enough to refill a Nevermore Micro (~10g) many times over. Made in the USA, packaged in Canada; also available in bulk on request. Price basis: 36.16 CAD at NorthPrint3D (~$25.38 USD at ~0.7018, Nov 13 2026).
Verdict Label: The standard refill carbon for Nevermore and BentoBox builds — buy a bag and stop paying per-filter prices
Cons:
Bulk consumable only — needs a filter unit (Nevermore, BentoBox, etc.) to be useful; not a filter on its own
No fan, housing, or printed parts included — just the media
Carbon saturates and must be replaced every few months with heavy use
400g bag is far more than a single small filter needs — overkill if you only own one Nevermore Micro
Pros:
High-porosity steam-activated anthracite carbon (1250–1300 m²/g surface area, CTC efficiency 80 minimum)
The standard refill carbon for Nevermore, Rebreather, and BentoBox filter designs
400g bag (~850mL) refills a Nevermore Micro (~10g) dozens of times — very low cost per refill
Acid-free, no sucrose-based binders; 4mm pellets for consistent bed packing
In stock at a Canadian vendor (NorthPrint3D), with bulk pricing available on request

Name: Nevermore StealthMax
Description: The Nevermore StealthMax is the high-capacity evolution of the Micro, designed for 300-350mm builds where the Micro's small carbon bed saturates too quickly. With 40-60g of carbon vs the Micro's ~10g, refill intervals are proportionally longer. The low-profile housing mounts in the same under-bed location without protruding visibly. Clear upgrade path recommendation: 250mm builds use the Micro; 300mm and larger should default to the StealthMax.
Verdict Label: The step-up for 300mm+ builds — larger carbon bed, longer service life between refills
Cons:
Larger print volume — more filament and print time to produce vs Micro
5015 blower adds to BOM vs the 4010s most builds already have on hand
Overkill for 250mm builds — the Micro is sufficient and simpler
Less community documentation than the Micro — newer design, fewer build logs
Pros:
Significantly larger carbon capacity (~40-60g) vs Micro (~10g) — notably longer life between carbon changes
Designed specifically for 300mm and 350mm build volumes where the Micro undersizes
Lower-profile 'stealth' geometry blends into the printer frame vs the visible Micro footprint
Single 5015 blower provides strong recirculation airflow across the larger carbon bed
Open source — STLs on GitHub, same community support network as Nevermore Micro

Name: HEPA Exhaust Mod
Description: HEPA exhaust mods are a general community pattern rather than a single product — multiple designers have published STLs that adapt standard 40mm or 80mm HEPA filter elements to printer exhaust ports. The approach captures ultrafine particles at the point of exhaust but does not recirculate or capture VOCs. Best for builders who can't exhaust outdoors and need some particulate reduction; for serious VOC reduction, pair with a Nevermore inside the enclosure.
Verdict Label: Documented community pattern for HEPA exhaust — implementation varies by printer model
Cons:
Exhaust-only filtration — air exits the printer rather than being recirculated and cleaned in-chamber
HEPA captures particles but does not address VOC/chemical fumes — no carbon stage
Multiple non-standard implementations exist; build quality varies significantly by remixer
Less effective than Nevermore+BentoBox combination for enclosed ABS printing
Pros:
Adds HEPA particulate filtration to any printer with an exhaust panel cutout
Standard 40×40mm or 80×80mm HEPA filter media — low cost, widely available for replacement
Adaptable pattern — community has versions for V2.4 exhaust panel, Trident, RatRig, and generic enclosures
Something rather than nothing for builders who can't or won't run Nevermore

Name: BentoBox
Description: The BentoBox is a two-stage air filtration unit designed by Rolohaun that mounts on the Voron gantry crossbar. It combines an activated carbon layer for VOC capture with a HEPA filter for ultrafine particle removal — the stage that Nevermore's carbon-only design doesn't address. Community framing is consistent: BentoBox and Nevermore Micro are complementary installs, not alternatives. The Nevermore handles continuous chamber VOC recirculation; the BentoBox adds the particulate filtration layer above it.
Verdict Label: Best paired with Nevermore — adds HEPA stage the carbon-only designs lack
Cons:
Not a standalone replacement for Nevermore — works best as a complement, not a substitute
Gantry mounting means the filter moves with the gantry — cable management consideration
Carbon capacity is modest vs dedicated carbon-only units
Higher print complexity than Nevermore Micro — more assembly steps
Pros:
Two-stage filtration: activated carbon VOC removal AND HEPA particulate capture in a single unit
HEPA stage catches ultrafine particles the Nevermore's carbon bed passes through
Mounts on the gantry crossbar — uses space that would otherwise be empty
Replacement HEPA filters are standard 40×40mm cut-to-size units — widely available
Open source by Rolohaun — active development, good community support

Name: Nevermore Micro v6
Description: The Nevermore Micro is the default air filtration recommendation for any Voron build. Rather than venting VOCs outside like the stock exhaust filter, it recirculates chamber air through an activated carbon bed — eliminating the need for outdoor exhaust routing entirely. The v6 design is the current standard, fits under the bed on both V2.4 and Trident without taking up enclosure panel real estate, and prints in a single session. Community consensus is clear: print this before you print anything else in ABS.
Verdict Label: Community consensus for Voron — the first mod everyone prints
Cons:
Carbon bed requires replacement every 2-4 months with heavy use — ongoing consumable cost
Fan not included — two 4010 fans must be sourced separately (already on most Voron BOM lists)
~8-12g carbon capacity is modest — the StealthMax is the upgrade path for larger builds
Small carbon volume can saturate faster when printing high-VOC materials like ABS all day
Pros:
Recirculates chamber air through activated carbon — eliminates VOCs rather than just venting them outside
Fits under the bed on V2.4 and Trident — no external panel cutout required
Dual 4010 axial fans provide consistent airflow across the carbon bed
Printed from ABS/ASA with the rest of the build — no sourcing from odd suppliers
Mature v6 design — well-documented, large community support, many remix variants

Name: Potassium Permanganate Impregnated Activated Alumina
Description: Potassium permanganate impregnated activated alumina — a chemical absorbent (chemisorbent) media for capturing VOCs, nitrogen dioxide, and some sulfur-containing compounds, similar to the community 'Nevermore Scorch' media. 3mm pellets, minimum 8% potassium permanganate content, 250 m²/g surface area. Sold as an 800g package (~850mL). Permanently absorbs VOCs; replace when the purple color degrades to gray or brown. NorthPrint3D recommends mixing with activated carbon for best results, noting carbon is less performant above 50°C. Handle with gloves and eyewear — it stains skin, clothes, and surfaces; hydrogen peroxide deactivates it. Price basis: 36.16 CAD at NorthPrint3D (~$25.38 USD at ~0.7018, Nov 13 2026).
Verdict Label: Niche chemical absorbent for VOCs carbon misses — worth it for heavy ABS/ASA printers, overkill for most builds
Cons:
Stains skin, clothes, and surfaces — gloves and eyewear required when handling
Not a standalone filter — must be loaded into a filter unit (e.g. Nevermore) and works best mixed with activated carbon
No published MSDS yet (listed as 'coming soon')
Niche media — most builders' VOC needs are met by plain activated carbon alone
Not carbon — do not confuse with activated carbon pellets; different media, different handling
Pros:
Chemisorbent media that permanently absorbs VOCs, nitrogen dioxide, and some sulfur-containing compounds carbon alone misses
Similar to the community 'Nevermore Scorch' media — a known upgrade path for Nevermore builds
800g package (~850mL) is a large quantity for the price
Color-change indicator — replace when purple degrades to gray or brown, no guessing
3mm pellets for low pressure drop across the filter bed

Name: Nevermore Duo
Description: The Nevermore Duo is the dual-fan variant of the Micro, delivering roughly twice the recirculation airflow. It targets builders running high-VOC schedules — continuous ABS or ASA printing where the Micro's single-fan airflow starts to fall short. For typical mixed-material Voron use, the Micro handles the job; the Duo is the answer when you're specifically saturating the Micro's capacity.
Verdict Label: Dual-fan variant for higher airflow — niche upgrade over the Micro for heavy ABS/ASA printers
Cons:
Wider footprint than Micro — verify bed clearance before printing
Two fans means two potential failure points and higher noise floor
For most builds and materials the Micro's airflow is sufficient — Duo is overkill unless running continuous ABS production
Less documented than the Micro — community build logs are sparse
Pros:
Dual 4010 fan configuration doubles airflow vs the single-fan Micro
Same activated carbon media as Micro — familiar carbon sourcing and replacement process
Useful for high-VOC print schedules (all-day ABS) where the Micro's flow rate falls short
Open source, same GitHub family as Micro
